holdingPanArchitectures.name: Deep Full-Size Hotel Pan (6-inch / 150mm Depth)
holdingPanArchitectures.description: Deep Gastronorm 1/1 stainless steel pan holding up to 20L of dense food (chili, refried beans, rice). The massive volume creates strong insulating inertia at the bottom, but the top 25–40mm experiences extreme evaporative cooling into ambient room air, dropping as low as 42°C–48°C even with well water at 75°C.

holdingPanArchitectures.name: Standard Full-Size Hotel Pan (4-inch / 100mm Depth)
holdingPanArchitectures.description: The standard buffet pan across institutional cafeterias and catering lines. Balances service volume with heat penetration. Without a fitted cover or regular stirring, surface evaporative drop exceeds 10°C within 45 minutes, dipping the upper boundary into the Bacillus cereus growth window.

holdingPanArchitectures.name: Shallow Hotel Pan (2.5-inch / 65mm Depth)
holdingPanArchitectures.description: Recommended by FDA Food Code annexes for temperature-sensitive items (fried rice, carved poultry, scrambled eggs). Shallow depth allows water bath steam heat to conduct rapidly through the entire food layer, keeping thermal stratification under 5°C throughout holding.

holdingPanArchitectures.name: Round Bain-Marie Soup Inset / Tureen (11-Quart / 10.5L)
holdingPanArchitectures.description: Cylindrical stainless steel tureen suspended deeply in circulating hot water. Reduced surface-to-volume ratio diminishes evaporative surface cooling compared to rectangular hotel pans, but viscous purees and chowders still stratify if not agitated with a ladle.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Cooked White Rice / Fried Rice / Cooked Pasta (Bacillus cereus Emetic Host)
foodMatrixProfiles.toxinType: Cereulide (Emetic Ring Depsipeptide - Heat Stable at 121°C)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Primary vehicle for Bacillus cereus emetic syndrome ('Fried Rice Syndrome'). Starch retrogradation forms moist insulating clumps with internal air gaps. When holding temperatures hover between 38°C and 52°C, heat-activated spores germinate and synthesize pre-formed cereulide toxin within 2 to 4 hours.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Dense Beef Chili / Brown Meat Gravy / Stew (C. perfringens Host)
foodMatrixProfiles.toxinType: Enterotoxin CPE (Pore-Forming Cytotoxin Released During Intestinal Sporulation)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Dense meat stews and bulk gravies cooked in large kettles drive out dissolved oxygen, establishing a deeply reduced anaerobic environment (Eh < -100 mV). Heat-tolerant C. perfringens spores survive boiling and germinate rapidly at 43°C–47°C, with doubling times under 10 minutes.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Clear Chicken Broth / Minestrone / Vegetable Consommé
foodMatrixProfiles.toxinType: Enterotoxins Hbl, Nhe & CytK (Heat-Labile Protein Enterotoxins)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Low viscosity enables natural convective fluid circulation across pan walls. Stratification is minimal as warm liquid rises from the base. However, if the steam well heater trips or thermostat fails below 57.2°C (135°F), vegetative B. cereus counts escalate steadily.

foodMatrixProfiles.name: Mashed Potatoes / Refried Beans / Thick Chowder Puree
foodMatrixProfiles.toxinType: Dual Sporeformer Hazard (Cereulide & C. perfringens CPE)
foodMatrixProfiles.description: Semi-solid consistency completely inhibits thermal convection. Heat transfer is purely conductive and exceptionally sluggish. The bottom 15mm touching the pan base can be 80°C while the core 50mm away lingers in the prime 40°C–50°C germination zone for entire 4-hour buffet shifts.

waterWellOperationalStates.name: Wet Water Bath at 78°C–82°C (172°F–180°F) - NSF/FDA Standard
waterWellOperationalStates.waterLevelStatus: Full Water Well (Water directly contacts pan bottom & lower sides)
waterWellOperationalStates.description: Optimal commercial standard. The steam table well is filled with clean potable water to 25mm below the rim. Condensing water vapor transfers latent heat with 95%+ thermal coupling across the stainless steel pan.

waterWellOperationalStates.name: Underheated Water Bath at 58°C–62°C (136°F–144°F) - Marginally Compliant
waterWellOperationalStates.waterLevelStatus: Adequate Water Level but Weak or Low Dial Setting
waterWellOperationalStates.description: Thermostat is dialed down to prevent food scorching or save electricity. While well water is technically above the 57.2°C (135°F) line, surface evaporative cooling drops the top food layer directly into the 44°C–50°C danger zone within 20 minutes.

waterWellOperationalStates.name: Dry Well Operation (Run Accidentally or Intentionally Without Water)
waterWellOperationalStates.waterLevelStatus: Completely Dry Well (Air-gap radiant heating only)
waterWellOperationalStates.description: Severe operational error. Without water, radiant air has poor heat capacity and terrible thermal conduction. Heating elements glow red-hot, scorching the bottom center of the pan (>110°C) while pan corners and upper food surface freeze into the 38°C–45°C pathogen incubator zone.

panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.name: Fitted Cover + Stirred Every 30 Minutes (FDA Gold Standard)
panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.description: Fitted stainless steel lid traps latent steam, maintaining relative humidity at 100% over the food surface and halting evaporative cooling. Stirring every 30 minutes homogenizes temperature throughout the entire pan depth.

panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.name: Fitted Cover + Unstirred Buffet Service
panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.description: Cover prevents severe moisture loss and keeps surface temperatures warm. However, in dense viscous purees, lack of agitation still permits a 6°C–8°C cool core in deep pans.

panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.name: Uncovered Open Display + Stirred Every 30 Minutes
panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.description: Common in fast-casual self-service lines where customers see the food. Significant surface evaporation occurs, but staff stir every 30 minutes, re-folding cooler surface crust back into the 75°C core before bacterial populations escalate.

panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.name: Uncovered Open Display + Unstirred (High-Risk Buffet Abuse)
panCoverageAndStirringProtocols.description: Extreme foodborne illness risk. Evaporative cooling drives surface temperature down by 15°C–22°C. A dehydrated skin forms over the pan, trapping an insulated layer below that sits at 42°C–48°C for hours—the biological optimum for Bacillus cereus cereulide synthesis.
